chosen.premise: Weezing is formed when two Koffing encounter different poison gases and fuse together over many years.
chosen.hook: Weezing may not be born—it may be two Koffing slowly fusing.
chosen.visualIdea: Show two Koffing drifting into different gas clouds, merging over a long timeline into one Weezing.
chosen.note: A highly specific origin story unique to Weezing, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries, with an excellent time-lapse fusion visual.

candidates.premise: Weezing’s twin bodies work like a seesaw: when one inflates, the other deflates while their gases mix.
candidates.hook: Weezing’s two bodies can’t inflate at the same time.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate one Weezing body swelling as the other shrinks, with arrows showing poisonous gas moving between them.
candidates.note: The seesaw-like body mechanic is concrete, distinctive, and strongly supported, though slightly less surprising to fans familiar with Weezing’s design.

candidates.premise: Weezing usually has two connected bodies, but rare triplets have been documented.
candidates.hook: Weezing normally comes in pairs—but rare triplets exist.
candidates.visualIdea: Reveal a standard two-bodied Weezing, then add a third body with a rarity warning and evidence-card overlay.
candidates.note: Rare triplets are an excellent obscure fact and strongly supported, though the triplet itself would need to be animated or composited because the supplied artwork does not show it.

candidates.premise: Weezing feeds on garbage gases, yet diluting the poison inside it can produce the highest-grade perfume.
candidates.hook: The Pokémon that feasts on garbage can make top-grade perfume.
candidates.visualIdea: Cut from Weezing inhaling a garbage cloud to a perfume bottle labeled as the highest grade.
candidates.note: The garbage-to-luxury-perfume contradiction is memorable and well supported, but the premise is more about an unusual use of Weezing than its core identity.

candidates.premise: Compared with Galarian Weezing, regular Weezing makes stronger toxins but cannot inhale air as effectively.
candidates.hook: Regular Weezing loses at breathing—but wins at poison potency.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen regular and Galarian Weezing: airflow drops on one side while a toxin meter rises.
candidates.note: The toxin-versus-airflow tradeoff is clearly supported and easy to visualize, but it depends on comparison with Galarian Weezing rather than revealing an especially obscure fact about regular Weezing alone.

candidates.premise: Weezing seeks out dirty, unkempt houses, moves in, and raids the trash while everyone sleeps.
candidates.hook: At night, Weezing breaks into homes—not for valuables, but for trash.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Weezing selecting a filthy house, sneaking through its rooms at night, and diving into a trash can.
candidates.note: Specific and cinematic, but 'breaks into homes' overstates the evidence: the entry says it inhabits dirty houses and goes through trash at night.

rounds.request: None; the fusion-origin angle is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific, surprising Weezing-only rule or contradiction with direct Pokédex support and a clear visual payoff.
